→ targeted re-scan of that bay · within the hour" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="42" width="390" x="15" y="92" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="b3" parent="biz" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#e1d5e7;strokeColor=#9673a6;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="order picked, ready for the floor

→ cleaning robot · IMMEDIATE, pre-empts everything" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="30" width="390" x="15" y="192" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="policy" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fffdf5;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=10;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=8;fontStyle=1" value="robot_task_policy — priority as REVIEWABLE DATA

Task priority is a BUSINESS decision, not a robotics one.
Same pattern as labour_rule (V02) and pricing_rule (I01) —
third time, which is itself an architectural slide." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="420" x="40" y="360" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="orch" parent="1" style="swimlane;startSize=34;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;fillColor=#f3faf1;strokeColor=#82b366;fontStyle=1;fontSize=12;fontColor=#3d7a2a;" value="robot-orchestration service (new, Java / Spring — OURS)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="230" width="440" x="520" y="100" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="o1" parent="orch" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;" value="task translation: business event → RMF task" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="40" width="400" x="20" y="44" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="o2" parent="orch" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;" value="priority + SLA policy per task type" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="40" width="400" x="20" y="92" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="o3" parent="orch" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f8cecc;strokeColor=#b85450;fontSize=11;fontStyle=1" value="R10 zone gate — PRE-FLIGHT, fail closed
task routes through a no_go / off_hours zone → REJECTED" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="46" width="400" x="20" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="o4" parent="orch" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;" value="outcome → ai_decision registry (I06)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="30" width="400" x="20" y="194" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="rmf" parent="1" style="swimlane;startSize=34;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;fillColor=#f3faf1;strokeColor=#82b366;fontStyle=1;fontSize=12;fontColor=#3d7a2a;" value="Open-RMF (Apache-2.0 · Intrinsic + OSRF · OSRA-governed since 2024)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="290" width="440" x="520" y="380" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="r1" parent="rmf" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;" value="traffic de-confliction · task allocation · lifts · doors" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="38" width="400" x="20" y="44" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="r2" parent="rmf" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;fontStyle=1" value="MUTEX GROUPS — virtual locks on routes and locations
that only one robot may occupy,
"mimicking air traffic control principles"" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="62" width="400" x="20" y="90" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="r3" parent="rmf" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;" value="automatic re-localisation after lift transit
→ "set and forget" multi-floor operation" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="48" width="400" x="20" y="160" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="r4" parent="rmf" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;" value="dynamic charger / parking assignment
by situational need, not fixed allocation" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="48" width="400" x="20" y="216" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="fleets" parent="1" style="swimlane;startSize=34;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;fillColor=#f9f9f9;strokeColor=#999999;fontStyle=1;fontSize=12;" value="Fleet adapters — two shapes" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="290" width="440" x="1020" y="100" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="f1" parent="fleets" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="Nav2-native robots
→ open-rmf/free_fleet over ZENOH
"if your robot exposes native ROS navigation
endpoints, it can be readily integrated"
⚠ zenoh config can filter and rate-limit by topic —
 store wifi is not warehouse ethernet" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="96" width="400" x="20" y="44" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="f2" parent="fleets" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=8;fontStyle=1" value="Vendor-API robots (Geek+, Pudu, Keenon)
→ full_control adapter from
 open-rmf/fleet_adapter_template

COPY THIS REFERENCE:
Ekumen-OS/andino_rmf — a production Nav2 ↔ RMF bridge" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="106" width="400" x="20" y="150" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="obl" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fffdf5;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=10;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=8;" value="What an adapter MUST implement — plan for all three

1 · KINEMATIC TRANSFORMATION
 facility map coords → robot local frame
 scale + rotation + offset
 reference_coordinates needs two sets of [x,y] for the
 SAME physical locations in both frames
 ⚠ minimum 4 matching waypoints recommended

2 · NAVIGATION COMMAND MAPPING
 high-level PathRequest → the robot's native actions

3 · STATE SYNCHRONISATION
 continuously publish FleetState (battery, mode, position)
 back to RMF with MINIMAL DELAY" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="250" width="440" x="1020" y="420" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="hw" parent="1" style="swimlane;startSize=34;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;fillColor=#f5f5f5;strokeColor=#999999;fontStyle=1;fontSize=12;" value="Mixed fleet — the hardware we do NOT build" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="290" width="270" x="1520" y="100" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="h1" parent="hw" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;fontSize=11;" value="Geek+ AMR
~56,000 units, RMS does 5,000 in one warehouse" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="52" width="240" x="15" y="44" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="h2" parent="hw" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;fontSize=11;" value="Pudu / Keenon service robot
#1 and #1 globally" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="52" width="240" x="15" y="106" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="h3" parent="hw" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;" value="shelf scanner (R01)
Nav2-native" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="52" width="240" x="15" y="168" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="h4" parent="hw" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;fontSize=11;" value="Quicktron / HAI
1,000 AMRs in one scenario" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="46" width="240" x="15" y="230" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="gap" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f3faf1;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=10;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=8;fontStyle=1" value="THE GAP

The research found NO retail-specific
Open-RMF integration — only warehouse
and facility deployments.

Retail sites have mixed fleets from
different vendors that do not talk
to each other.

Gartner: by 2026 &gt;40% of enterprises
will require cross-brand scheduling." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="250" width="270" x="1520" y="420" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="line" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f9f9f9;strokeColor=#999999;fontSize=12;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=middle;dashed=1;" value="Line in the sand: we translate business intent into robot tasks and report outcomes. NOT warehouse task management, NOT inventory logic, NOT robot control, NOT a WMS.
Versions: core RMF supports ROS 2 Humble / Iron / Jazzy on distro-specific branches; examples target ros-jazzy-nav2-bringup. Use binaries unless you are patching RMF itself.
Safety is deliberately NOT here — R10 owns it, and shipping a fleet orchestrator without a safety gate is the wrong order." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="100" width="1750" x="40" y="720" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="metric" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f3faf1;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=12;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=middle;fontStyle=1" value="The metric that justifies the layer: CROSS-FLEET CONFLICTS AVOIDED. Plus tasks completed per robot-hour, deadlock/contention events, task latency by type, robot utilisation." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="70" width="1750" x="40" y="850" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> div.div:
What an adapter MUST implement — plan for all three
1 · KINEMATIC TRANSFORMATION
facility map coords → robot local frame
scale + rotation + offset
reference_coordinates needs two sets of [x,y] for the
SAME physical locations in both frames
⚠ minimum 4 matching waypoints recommended
2 · NAVIGATION COMMAND MAPPING
high-level PathRequest → the robot's native actions
3 · STATE SYNCHRONISATION
continuously publish FleetState (battery, mode, position)
back to RMF with MINIMAL DELAY

div.div:
THE GAP
The research found NO retail-specific
Open-RMF integration — only warehouse
and facility deployments.
Retail sites have mixed fleets from
different vendors that do not talk
to each other.
Gartner: by 2026 >40% of enterprises
will require cross-brand scheduling.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1736px; height: 1px; padding-top: 750px; margin-left: 14px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Line in the sand: we translate business intent into robot tasks and report outcomes. NOT warehouse task management, NOT inventory logic, NOT robot control, NOT a WMS.
Versions: core RMF supports ROS 2 Humble / Iron / Jazzy on distro-specific branches; examples target ros-jazzy-nav2-bringup. Use binaries unless you are patching RMF itself.
Safety is deliberately NOT here — R10 owns it, and shipping a fleet orchestrator without a safety gate is the wrong order.
